problems.label: Distressing unusual experiences and a drop in daily functioning
definitions: Hears voices or holds beliefs that cause fear or distress and that others do not share.
Has had trouble keeping up with work, study or self-care over recent months.
Has pulled away from family and friends.
longTermGoals: The client feels safer and less distressed by the experiences, stays connected to care, and returns to valued roles such as work, study and relationships.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 1 week, complete a referral to an early psychosis or coordinated specialty care program, or to psychiatry, and attend the first appointment.
Attend medication appointments and bring questions about benefits and side effects to each visit.
By week 8, start CBT for psychosis, and develop at least 2 coping strategies for distressing voices or thoughts.
With consent, involve family in at least 4 family sessions over 3 months, focused on information, communication and an early-warning plan.
Keep a regular sleep schedule and take a 20-minute walk or other activity at least 3 days a week for 4 weeks.
By session 2, complete a written safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people and services to contact, and steps to make the home safer, and review it at least monthly.
Complete the PHQ-9 at intake and every 4 weeks, and review mood and safety at each session.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
